Because PCI is performed with the patient under local anes-
thesia in a cardiac catheterization laboratory, recovery is quicker 
than with coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery. In 
CABG surgery, an artery from the chest is used to redirect blood 
flow around a diseased vessel. Candidates for CABG usually 
have more than two occluded arteries. CABG surgeries have 
decreased since 1995 because more PCI procedures are being 
done. These surgeries improve survival time, relieve symptoms, 
and markedly improve the quality of life for patients with 
ASCVD. However, CABG does not cure atherosclerosis; the new 
grafts are also susceptible to atherogenesis. Consequently, reste-
nosis is common within 10 years of surgery.
